programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha na h-Abadas air a bhith trang a' togail caisteal-sneachd 's iad a-nis a' coimhead air n-adhart ri geama a chluich. 'S e Hari a tha a' lorg am facal an-diugh 's e am broinn an taighe. After building a snow castle in the mountains, the Abadas settle down with Ben for the word game. Soon, Hari is sent to look for a stool inside the house.

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Nuair a lorgas Sif, Pipp agus Bran sreang-fhiacaill, tha farpais tarraing ròpa air fàire! Ziff, Pipp and Button discover dental floss and plan an exciting tug-of-war showdown!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Meanbh Chlangair 's a caraidean Lusach, a' cluich ceòl còmhla ris na Craobhan Ciùil. Dè tha siud? Tha cuideigin eile ri seinn cuideachd. Saoil cò th' ann? Tiny Clanger and her flower friends are making music with the Music Trees. What’s that? Someone else is singing, too. Who could it be?

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona ‘s Otto a' cur romhpa a dhol a choimhead Leum a’ Bhradain ach mus fhaigh iad falbh, feumaidh Otto Pip ‘s Pop a chur dhan leabaidh às-dèidh an t-sealg-oidhch'. Ge-tà, chan eil e coltach g’ eil na cailleachan-oidhche bheaga idir sgìth. Oona and Otto decide to spend the morning watching the 'salmon leap' but before they can set off, Otto must put Pip and Pop to bed after the night hunt. Unfortunately for Otto, it doesnt seem that the young owls are in the least bit tired.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha farspach a’ nochdadh air a’ chreag agus i ann an sunnd airson mi-mhodh. Ge-tà, nuair a dh’fheuchas i ri biadh a ghoid bho fhaoileag bhìodach, tha Oona ‘s Baba a' tighinn na h-aghaidh gus an t-ìsean a dhìon! The great gull has made her way to Puffin Rock and is intent on causing all sorts of mischief. However, when she sets her sights on a poor little seagul chick, Oona and Baba are ready to challenge her and protect the little bird!

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc: Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Rose agus na mialchoin aice, Libby is Marvin. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh coin agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Rose is na coin a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean. Eilidh Cormack visits Rose and her beautiful greyhound dogs, Libby and Marvin. We learn how to look after dogs and find out about all the lovely stuff they get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home; including how best to handle, train and feed them.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ leughadh Norton agus Alpha. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Kristyna Litten agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Niall Iain Macdonald reads Norton agus Alpha, written and illustrated by Kristyna Litten and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha sinn air ais ann an Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche airson teirm ùr. Tha tòrr air tachairt thairis air na saor-làithean. Cha robh an là in-sheirbheis cho soirbheachail `s a bha Maighstir Mackle an dùil agus tha Ms Sharpe air nochdadh sna pàipearan-naidheachd ri linn ‘s na thachair aig a’ Mhòd. Our cameras are back at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche for a new term. A lot has happened over the holidays. The in-service day wasn’t as successful as Mr Mackle had hoped and Ms Sharpe has made the newspapers after what happened at the Mòd.

programme.title: Aidan: Balach Beag Muay Thai
programme.desc: Tha Aidan ag ullachachadh airson sabaid mhòr aig Farpais Muay Thai na Cruinne. Aidan prepares to compete in the biggest Muay Thai fight of his life.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha Sebastian cho toilicht’ nuair a tha e a’ faighinn seann leabhar-latha beanntan Chaspair – leabhar air leth sònraicht’. Gu mì-fhortanach ge-tà, tha Mgr. Turner ga thoirt bhuaithe, mar pheanas. Ciamar a gheibh e air seo innnse do Chaspair? Sebastian is so happy when he gets Caspar’s old mountain journal, a very special book. Unfortunately, Mr Turner confiscates it as a punishment. How can he tell Caspar about this?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha Bitzer air fois fhaighinn agus Seonaidh bochd fo gheasaibh aig Mowermouth an Gobhair. Ge-tà leis an treud air fad fo smachd Mowermouth, tha Bitzer a' tuigse gu bheil feum aige air a dheagh charaid. Bitzer gets his wish for some peace and quiet when Shaun becomes hypnotised by Mowermouth the goat and finally stops bothering him. But with the whole flock under the influence of Mowermouth's powerful gaze, Bitzer soon realises just how much he needs his old buddy.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: A chocolate babka is a feast for the eyes as well as the belly! It's a popular dish in Poland and the Ukraine. Tha babka teòclaid taitneach, an dà chuid dhan bhrù agus dhan t-sùil! Tha fèill air anns a' Phòlaind agus anns a' Ucràin. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Fonn mo Bheatha
programme.desc: Music and chat programme presented by Cathy Ann MacPhee, with guest Calum Alex MacMillan. Ceòl agus còmhradh le Cathy Ann Nic a Phi còmhla ri Calum Ailig MacMhaolain. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc: Green-fingered Murdo Macdonald visits some of the country’s most important gardens to explore their design, plant-life, setting and history. Murdo explores Benmore Botanic Garden near Dunoon in Argyll. He visits the Victorian fernery, the Tasmanian Ridge and the Chilean Rainforest Glade where he plants a monkey puzzle tree. Dr Mark Newman of the Royal Botanic Garden, Edinburgh, tells us about the important role of botanic gardens in conservation and education. Tha gàirneilear sgileil, Murchadh Dòmhnallach, a’ tadhal air cuid de ghàrraidhean mòra na h-Alba, a’coimhead air an cruth, na tha fàs unnta agus an eachdraidh. Sa phrògram seo tha Murchadh a’gabhail chuairt tro Ghàrradh Luibheanach na Beinne Mòire faisg air Dùn Omhain ann an Earra-Ghaidheal. Tha e a’faicinn a’chruinneachadh rainich, a thòisich san naoitheamh linn deug, agus chì e earrainn den ghàrradh an riochd Tasmania agus cuideachd ceò-choille Chile, far a bheil e fhèin a’cur craobh monkey-puzzle. Innsidh an t-Oll. Mark Newman bho Ghàrradh Luibheanach Rìoghail Dhùn-Èidinn dhuinn cho cudromach sa tha gàrraidhean luibheanach a thaobh glèidhteachas agus foghlam. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Seo an fharpais-cheist far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Presented by Niall Iain MacDonald, this is the quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Playing from the comfort of their own homes are the Pretenders, and they are the ones posing the questions! Battling them to win the big prize in the studio are Ewen and Jonny, and Marley and Denise. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.desc: Skipinnish le The Atholl Set ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform The Atholl Set in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha tòrr spòrs aig Peicein is a charaidean a’ cur an ìre gur e ròbotan a th’ annta, gus am brùth cuideigin aca putan is tha an aileag a’ tòiseachadh air Peicein. Carson nach stad an aileag aige? Bheil smachd aig cuideigin air à àiteigin eile? Chan urrainn do Ghriogair sguir a shreothartaich, Lòra a mhèaranaich neo Raghnall a chasadaich. Saoil a bheil iad uile a’ tionndadh nan ròbotan dhà-rìribh? Petit and his friends are having a lot of fun pretending to be robots, until one of them presses a button and Petit gets the hiccups. Why can't he stop hiccupping? Is someone else controlling him from somewhere? Greg can't stop sneezing, Laura yawns and Roman coughs. Could it be that everyone is turning into real life robots?

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc: Tha Rita agus Pompon airson fàilte bhlàth a thoirt do Shìthiche nam Fiaclan ach, gu mì-fhortanach, nuair a tha Pompon a' dùsgadh, chan eil ach aon phrèasant ri fhaicinn. Saoil cò gheibh am prèasant? Rita and Pompon want to welcome the Tooth Fairy but, unfortunately, when Pompon wakes up, only one present has been left. Who do you think gets the present?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha a h-uile duine air an sàrachadh is cùisean cho dòrainneach. Tha Àtaidh a’ togail trèana airson is gun urrainn dhaibh uile a dhol air turas. An uair sin tha beachd aig Tilidh, is tha i a’ moladh gun tèid iad uile air turas timcheall an eilein air fad. ’S e turas air leth a th’ ann, gus an tig rudeigin nan rathad! Everybody is bored. Abney builds a train so they can go on a tour. Then Teal has an idea: why don’t they tour the whole island? It is a fantastic tour until something gets in the way!

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Nuair a chì Sionnach mar a tha Feòrag air a beò-ghlacadh le na saor-làithean mìorbhaileach aice anns a’ choille, tha e fhèin airson a dhol air saor-làithean. Chan eil Maigheach cho cinnteach mun chùis. Cò choimheadas às dèidh a’ bhothain agus a’ ghàrraidh? Cò ach Tosg is Comhachag! Carson nach rachadh an dithis aca-san air saor-làithean mìorbhaileach anns a’ bhothan? Saoil dè cho mìorbhaileach ’s a bhios na saor-làithean aca uile? Brush really enjoys her holiday in the forest, which makes Fox want to go on one as well! Hare isn’t so sure - who will take care of their den and garden? Well, Tusk and Owl of course! Fox and Hare convince them to stay in their den and have a good break, too. Will everybody’s holiday turn out as 'wonnnnderful' as they hope?

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.desc: Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Alistair Heather leis a’ chuid as fheàrr bho Na Trads 2025 à Talla-ciùil Obar Dheathain. Le ceòl bho Mec Lir, Màiri NicAonghais, Rory Matheson Dance Band, Ellie Beaton agus Ross Miller Band am measg gu leòr eile, agus còmhradh le buannaichean is rionnagan an tachartais – an dà chuid air an àrd-ùrlar agus air cùl gnothaich. programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram sònraichte air DiDòmhnaich Cuimhneachaidh. Salm 124 air a sheinn le Ceòlraidh Ghàidhlig Ghlaschu, an laoidh Nam Aonar le Mo Smuaintinn le Còisir Ghàidhlig Ìleach Ghlaschu agus bidh An t-Urr. Aonghas Mac a' Ghobhainn ag innse mun àite a th' aig creideamh an lùib cogadh is call. Tha am prògram air aithris le Iain MacFhionghain. A special programme for Remembrance Sunday, with Psalm 124 sung by Glasgow Gaelic Choir and the hymn Nam Aonar le mo Smuaintinn by Glasgow Islay Gaelic Choir. Rev Angus Smith describes the part faith plays in war and loss. Presented by Iain MacKinnon.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets singer Mary Ann Kennedy in Ardgour. Although born in Glasgow, Mary Ann discusses how she has made her home in Ardgour and what that means to her. As they walk along Cona Glen, Mary Ann opens up about feeling comfortable in her own skin and how the environment has helped her find peace. She chats about her changing relationship with music and what brings her happiness. San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha. Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri Màiri Anna NicUalraig ann an Àird Ghobhar. Ged a rugadh i ann an Glaschu, innsidh Mairi Anna an luach a tha i cuir air far a bheil i air a dachaigh a steidheachadh. A ’coiseachd tron Chona Ghleann, fuasglaidh Màiri Anna suas ma beachdan air a pearsa fhèin agus mar a tha an àrainneachd mu chuairt air a cuideachadh gus sìth a lorg. Tha conaltradh ann ma caochladh dhàimh le ceòl agus dè dìreach a tha toirt toileachas dhi. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Actress turned interior designer Erica Macpherson takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers, she finds new ideas for designing old spaces. Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Nic a’ Phersain, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc: Calum explores the underground sites of central Scotland. First, author Mairi Kidd introduces him to a lesser known history of Edinburgh below the city streets. Then he ventures under the busy platforms of Glasgow Central Station, where Calum discovers an atmospheric disused Victorian platform. In Dunoon, Calum gets help from his friend Kenny Rankin to access the Paper Caves and find out more about a story that dates back almost 350 years, connecting the Campbell clan with the site. ’S a’ phrògram mu dheireadh, nì Calum rannsachadh air làraich fon talamh ann am meadhan na h-Alba. Innsidh an t-ùghdair, Màiri Kidd, dha mun eachdraidh fo shràidean Dhùn Èideann air nach eil mòran eòlach. Fo àrd-ùrlairean trang Stèisean Rèile Meadhan Ghlaschu, gheibh Calum lorg air àrd-ùrlar iongantach, neo-chleachte bho linn Bhictòiria. Ann an Dùn Omhain, bheir a charaid, Coinneach MacFhraing, cuideachadh do Chalum gus Uamhan nam Pàipear a ruighinn agus tuilleadh ionnsachadh mu sgeulachd bhon t-seachdamh linn deug a tha a’ ceangal na Caimbeulaich ris an t-sreath uamhan seo. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Air fhilmeadh aig àm Celtic Connections 2024 agus a’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh a dh’aona ghothach airson Seirm, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Kathryn Tickell & The Darkening, Eòghann MacEunraig, Genticorum, TEUD & Kaïa Kater. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2024, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Kathryn Tickell & The Darkening, Ewen Henderson, Genticorum and intimate session recordings with TEUD & Kaïa Kater. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: Rannsachadh air na dòighean annasach a tha fradharc bheathaichean air leasachadh. An exploration of the strange evolution of animal vision.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le The Island ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform The Island in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean ag ionnsachadh dè tha gabhail àite fon talamh – air leth inntinneach! Daolag-bhreac and Seillean are learning what happens underground - really interesting!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha a’ ghrian a’ deàrrsadh ‘s tha Ooona'son dhol a dh’iasgach. Tha May ag aontachadh cluich cuide ri Baba ach tha Baba a’ diùltadh faiche nan gràineag fhàgail gus an dùisg Spiky bho chadal-geamhraidh! It’s a beautiful day and Oona wants to practise fishing. May offers to play with Baba, who refuses to leave the hedghog burrow as he wants to wait until Spiky wakes from his hibernation!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona daonnan ann an cabhag ach tha Papa airson sealltainn dhi gum bi buthaidean a' gabhail cùisean air an socair. Saoil an tig aice air ionnsachadh rudan a dhèanamh ann an ‘Dòigh na Buthaide? Oona is forever in a hurry to learn and get things done, but Papa wants to show her that puffins tend to approach things in a slow and steady fashion. Will Oona master the ‘Way of the Puffin?’

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Nuair tha Fuigheag acrach a’ chiad char sa mhadainn, tha e feumach air biadh. Ach ciamar a gheibh e sin ‘s Boban na shuain chadail? When Fuigheag is hungry first thing in the morning, he needs food. But how will he get some with Boban fast asleep?

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Le cuideachadh bho Burtaidh, tha Sif a’ toirt Pipp agus Bran air dàn-chuairt fèill spòrs. Ziff leads Pipp and Button on a fairground adventure with help from faithful Bertie.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Tha Sionnach airson ’s gum bi co-là-breith sònraichte aig Maigheach. Tha cuireadh aig Comhachag is Tosg, fhad ’s a bheir iad prèasant brèagha thuice, leithid dìthean le fàileadh cùbhraidh. Chan eil sin cho furasta ’s a shaoileas iad. Fhad ’s a tha iad trang a’ lorg nam prèasantan tha Maigheach air bhioran ’s I a’ feitheamh gus an tòisich am pàrtaidh co-là-breith aice. Fox wants to give Hare the best birthday ever. Owl and Tusk are invited, but only if they bring a nice present, like a beautifully scented flower. But that is not quite as easy as it seems. All the while Hare is kept waiting for her birthday party to start.

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Pompon 's a phàrantan ag ullachadh 'son turas air falbh, feumaidh Pompon tighinn gu co-dhùnadh air dè tha riatanach a thoirt leis sa bhaga aige. When Pompon and his parents prepare to go on a trip, Pompon must come to a decision as to what is essential for him to take in his bag.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ leughadh Famh agus Èirigh-na-grèine. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Jeanne Willis agus a dhealbhachadh le Sarah Fox-Davies. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Eilidh Cormack reads Famh agus Èirigh-na-grèine by Jeanne Willis, illustrated Sarah Fox-Davies and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: SpongeBob
programme.desc: Heat-loving hippies move into Mr Krabs' soup vat! Tha sgioba an tòir air blàths a’ lorg dachaigh anns a’ bhrot aig Mgr. Crùbag.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha sgrudaire sgoile air nochdadh aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche agus chan eil Maighstir Mackle neo na tidsearan deiseil air a shon. Chan eil cùisean a’ coimhead ro mhath do Mhaighstir MhicFhraing ach tha Maighstir Strachan air a chasan, neo co-dhiù aona chois a lorg. Dè as urrainn a dhol ceàrr?! There’s a surprise visit from a school inspector at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche. It’s not looking good for Mr MacFhraing, although Mr Strachan seems to have found his feet, well one foot at least. What could possibly go wrong?!

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc: Nuair tha Greta an cù a’ cèilidh air an sgoil, tha Flix airson a bhith taiceil dhi. Gu mì-fhortanach tha iad glè mhì-mhodhail nuair a tha ‘ad còmhla. Tha seo ag adhbharachadh trioblaid coin-cait ach the feum air fuasgladh cait-coin. When Greta the dog visits the school, Flix wants to be helpful to her. Unfortunately, they’re very badly behaved when together. This causes a dog-cat problem so what’s needed is a cat-dog solution!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Sona air a bhith trang a’ fàsgadh dhearcan ach tha e air cus den t-sùgh òl – tha sin ga fhàgail nas beòthail’ ‘s nas toilicht’ na bha e o chionn fhada. Abair gu bheil deagh ghumbladh a’ gabhail àit’! Sona has been busy pulping berries but he’s drunk too much of the juice - this has made him livelier and happier than he’s been for quite a while. There’s a lot of Gumbling taking place!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha an dithis mhealltair – Merri is Seonaidh – ri miastadh. Nuair a tha ’ad a' toirt seachad gheallaidhean nach meall ’ad na Gumbalan, tha ’ad a' tionndadh gus feuchainn ris a’ char a thoirt às na Bògaisean. Saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh? The two tricksters, Merri and Seonaidh, are up to no good. When they promise not to trick the Gumbals, they turn to playing mischief on the Bògaisean. How will they get on?

programme.title: Fillte
programme.desc: Fillte travels throughout Scotland, visiting the country’s finest woven craft producers. Tha Fillte a siuhbail fad Alba a lorg an obair-laimhne is fhearr, sa luchd-ciùird fighe a chruthaich e.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: We meet Gaelic learner Caroline Quinn from Trinidad and Tobago, while Calum Maclean is in Portmahomack, Easter Ross, learning about his heritage.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Farpais-cheist do-chreidsinneach... Mas Fhìor! Le ochdnar Mas Fhìoraich a’ cluich bhon dachaighean fhèin, ’s iad an fheadhainn a chuireas na ceistean agus na freagairtean. An urrainn do Isla is Hamish agus Jamie is Liam a tha a’ cluich bhon stiùideo a’ chùis a dhèanamh orra airson an duais mhòr a bhuannachadh? A quiz show that is pretty unbelievable! Eight Pretenders play from the comfort of their own homes and hold all the questions and answers to this quiz. Can Isla and Hamish, or Jamie and Liam in the studio beat the Pretenders for a chance to win a cash prize? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Tha Cathy Nicdhòmhnaill a’ bruidhinn ri clann a’ mhansa an là an-diugh. Cathy Macdonald talks to children of the manse.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: The arrival of potential Norwegian investor Johan throws a cat among the pigeons as age old family secrets and resentments come to the fore. The MacSween clan soon begin to realise that the mill is in worse shape than they thought and Seumas makes a surprise announcement to save the mill. Tha ruighinn, an neach-tasgaidh Nirribheach Johan a’ cur a' chiùil air feadh na fìdhle. Tha rùintean-dìomhair agus seann nàimhdeas an teaghlaich a’ togail ceann aon uair eile. Chan eil e a’ toirt fad sam bith mus tuig teaghlach MhicSuain gu bheil a’ mhuileann ann an staid fada nas miosa na bha iad an dùil agus tha a’ bheachd a th’ aig Seumas airson a’ mhuileann a shàbhaileadh a’ cur iongnadh orra uile. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.desc: Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ dol air turas gus faighinn a-mach mun chrìoch eadar an Spàinn agus Moroco. Ann an Ceuta tha feansa àrd a’ sgaradh Afraga agus an Roinn Eòrpa agus dha mòran is e seo an geata chun na Roinn Eòrpa. Coinnichidh Ramsay ri imrichean a tha air a h-uile càil a tha aca a chuir ann an cunnart is iad a’ dol tarsainn air a’ bhalla an tòir air beatha nas fheàrr. Cluinnidh e bho luchd-còmhnaidh ionadail Ceuta a tha beò fo sgàil teannachadh poilitigeach agus coinnichidh e ri daoine a bhios ag obair gus an fheadhainn as motha a th’ ann an cunnart a chuideachadh. Ramsay MacMahon goes on a journey to find out about the border between Spain and Morocco. In Ceuta, a high fence separates Africa and Europe, and for many, this is the gateway to Europe. Ramsay meets migrants who have risked everything to cross the wall in the hope of a better life. He hears from local residents who live with the political tensions and meets people who work to help the most vulnerable. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le The Poozies le Wired to the Moon agus Sausage. Clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads 2025 ann an Obar Dheathain. Concert set performed by The Poozies, featuring the tracks Wired to the Moon and Sausage. Originally recorded live at the 2025 Trad Awards in Aberdeen.

programme.title: OMC!
programme.desc: Sketch show featuring a collection of comic characters and spoofs. Written by and starring the very best in emerging and established comic talent. Featuring Iain Beggs, Darren Maclean, Carina Macleod, Claire Frances MacNeil, Hannah McKirdy, Lana Pheutan and David Walker. Includes the latest updates from the ferry office, a recipe with a difference, and red hot passion finds physical expression via a clown love triangle. Anns an ceithreamh prògram bho shreath ùr OMC! chì sinn tuilleadh sgeidsichean loma-làn charactaran èibhinn, suidheachaidhean neònach agus ‘spoofs’ gun shamhail bho na sgriobhadariean is cleasaichean as fheàrr a th’ann. Gheibh sinn an turas sa beachd car eadar-dhealaichte airson reasabaidh, tha cridhe Doodles an cleasaiche a’ briseadh agus, ’s e cheist as motha an t-seachdan sa, am bidh an aiseig a’ seòladh? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: Professor Ben Garrod explores how some snakes can see using heat, how crocodiles feel through their jaws and how some animals use electricity to navigate their world - and it is all only possible because of remarkable adaptations to their skin. Whether animals live on land, in the sea, or in subterranean communities, skin is critical in allowing them to sense the world around them, be it to find food, navigate harsh environments or avoid danger. Even the toughest of animals, crocodilians, have a surprisingly sensitive side when it comes to the specialised skin sensors they use to detect the tiniest of ripples in the water. Deadly pit vipers use heat sensors to ambush the small rodents they feed on. Professor Ben Garrod puts them to the test with an experiment to see if they will strike a cold or warm ping-pong ball. He also uncovers how the less-than-attractive leaf-nosed bat puts its facial skin to good use as an acoustic lens to echolocate around its dense forest habitat.

programme.title: Cornwall's Red River
programme.desc: Poet John Wedgwood Clarke explores the Red River in Cornwall, a watercourse barely more than a stream that has been heavily polluted by centuries of tin mining. Now, this powerful symbol of Cornish identity, home to some very rare, beautiful and resilient species, is slowly showing signs of coming back to life. Extracts from John's poem, Red River at the A30 Culvert, reveal his mixed thoughts about the river's toxic legacy, but as he meets both those with a connection with the river's industrial past and who care for it today, he finds new hope for its future.

programme.title: What Are UFOs?
programme.desc: For decades, UFOs have intrigued the world, but many scientists avoided studying them. In the United States, after highly publicised sightings of unidentified objects by US Navy pilots, UFOs are moving out of the shadows and into the light as NASA pledges to study them scientifically. So what does science have to say? Though some are identified as balloons, drones, weather phenomena or optical illusions, others remain mysterious. Could they be the result of secret new technology? And what would it take for alien engineers to traverse vast distances to send probes or visit Earth from other solar systems? Explore the evidence as astrophysicists and engineers use new technologies to investigate the strangest objects in our skies.

programme.title: Mark Lawson Talks To...
programme.desc: Master of horror writing Stephen King talks to Mark Lawson about his book Lisey's Story and discusses the inspiration for his novels and how he battled with his own demons.

programme.title: Singer-Songwriters at the BBC
programme.desc: The celebration of the singing songwriting troubadours of the 1960s and 70s continues with a further trawl through the BBC archives for timeless and classic performances. Don McLean performs his huge hit American Pie from 1972 and Tim Buckley provides some sublime sounds with a rendition of his song Happy Time. Also making an appearance is the long-lamented John Martyn, folk queen Sandy Denny and, in a duet with Joe Egan as Stealers Wheel, the late Gerry Rafferty. Stealers Wheel chum and one-time collaborator Rab Noakes also makes a contribution to this compilation. Leonard Cohen and Julie Felix present a unique collaboration and performance of Hey, That's No Way to Say Goodbye, and there's an unforgettable performance of Case of You by Joni Mitchell. No celebration of this genre would be complete without contributions from songwriting heavyweights such as Elton John, Paul Simon, Loudon Wainwright III and Yusuf Islam aka Cat Stevens.

programme.title: Singer-Songwriters at the BBC
programme.desc: The celebration of the singing songwriting troubadours of the 1960s and 70s continues with a further trawl through the BBC archives for timeless and classic performances. Tom Paxton starts proceedings with a rare black and white performance of his classic song The Last Thing on My Mind filmed in 1964. Also making an appearance is the 'fifth Beatle', Harry Nilsson, with a performance from his BBC concert in 1972. Other gems from this year include Canadian Gordon Lightfoot, songwriting duo Gerry Rafferty and Joe Egan as Stealers Wheel and the most popular acoustic act of the 1970s, the gentle, bespectacled John Denver. From the Basil Brush Show in 1973, Ronnie Lane and Slim Chance make a surprise appearance. Californian Beach Boy Bruce Johnston offers a sublime version of Disney Girls, and Joan Armatrading injects a bit of brio on the Old Grey Whistle Test. Rounding it all off is six-time Grammy winner Billy Joel.

programme.desc: Francois Truffaut's classic revenge thriller. Julie Kohler sets out to track down, charm and kill five men who do not know her. One by one, she ticks their names off her list. But what is her goal? In French with English subtitles.

programme.desc: Mark Cousins talks to French actress Jeanne Moreau in Paris about her career as they look at clips from her films.

programme.title: Omnibus

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: The BBC's 2025 ghost story for Christmas, Mark Gatiss's adaptation of EF Benson's The Room in the Tower. It's 1944, and while sheltering during an air raid, Roger strikes up a conversation with Verity, a Wren. When he asks if she dreams, he begins to recount the haunting vision that has followed him for most of his life: a recurring dream of a mysterious house, a silent family on the lawn and an unseen, unidentified terror lurking in the room in the tower. But when he is invited to stay at a country estate eerily similar to the one in his dreams, and is assigned the very same room, he becomes increasingly disturbed as his nightmares begin to become reality. What is really waiting for him in the room in the tower?

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: In her final days, Edith Nesbit recounts the chilling tale of newlywed Victorians Jack and Laura. As they settle into a small cottage in a quiet village, they soon find their idyll overshadowed by the superstitious warnings of their housekeeper and the legend of two marble tomb effigies who are said to rise each year and walk. Jack dismisses this is as mere folklore. But as the fateful night draws near, he makes a terrifying discovery. And back at the cottage, Laura is all alone...

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: It’s 1881, and Old College, Oxford plays host to three very different academics. Abercrombie Smith is a model of Victorian manhood, clean of limb and sound of mind. Monkhouse Lee is a delicate and unworldly student from Thailand. And occupying the rooms between them is the strange and exotic Edward Bellingham, whose unnatural researches into the secrets of ancient Egypt are the talk of the college. Can Bellingham’s experiments truly bring the breath of life to the horrifying bag of bones that is the mysterious Lot No 249?

programme.title: Secret Knowledge
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley tells the story of Bolsover Castle in Derbyshire. Built in the early 17th century, it became the pleasure palace of playboy Cavalier and ambitious courtier William Cavendish. Guiding us on a tour of the castle and its remarkable collection of artworks, Lucy brings to life the spectacular masque held by Cavendish to win the favour of King Charles I. And from within the walls of this eccentric architectural gem emerges a colourful tale, capturing the tensions of early 17th-century England that would eventually lead the nation to civil war.

programme.title: War Grave

programme.title: Playing the Dane
programme.desc: Stars of theatre, television and film, including Jeremy Brett, Steven Berkoff, Richard Briers, Christopher Plummer, Ian McKellen and Christopher Walken, describe the challenge of playing Shakespeare's Hamlet.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: In 1964, a young Steven Berkoff was cast in one of his earliest screen roles, as a junior player in Hamlet in Elsinore, a BBC co-production with Danish television. Shot in Denmark by director Philip Saville, it starred Christopher Plummer as Hamlet and Michael Caine, in his only Shakespeare role, as Horatio. Here, Berkoff shares his memories of the production and how he got involved, gives his verdict on how the film stands up today and describes - as only he can - the excitement and inspiration he felt from watching Plummer and Caine at work.

programme.title: Hamlet at Elsinore
programme.desc: 1964 production of Shakespeare's famous play. Filmed in Elsinore, Denmark.

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: Sweden, 1863. A country not much visited by Englishmen. An exception is the inquisitive Mr Wraxhall, whose innocent rummaging through the archives of the noble de la Gardie family takes a sinister turn. Wraxhall becomes fascinated by the long-dead founder of the dynasty, the fearsome Count Magnus, a tyrannical ruler who dabbled in alchemy and who once made a strange journey to the Holy Land on most unholy business. Despite the warnings of his hosts, Wraxhall is drawn ever deeper into the Count’s dark world and discovers that the dreaded aristocrat may not lie easy in his tomb...

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: 1923. Edward Williams, gentleman and amateur golfer, lives an untroubled life as the curator of a small university museum. His speciality is the topography of the British Isles. So when an art dealer sends him details of an interesting engraving - a mezzotint - of an old country house, he’s intrigued. When the picture arrives, however, it seems perfectly ordinary - until Williams notices a figure in the picture where there was none before. A cloaked figure, with a skull-like head and legs that are horribly thin. Soon, within the mezzotint, the figure seems to be on the move across the moonlit lawn towards the house with murderous intent. Long-forgotten secrets rise to the surface as Williams and his friends summon all the rational forces at their command to confront the impossible.

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: Adaptation of a ghost story by MR James. 1684. John Martin is on trial for his life. Facing him, the infamous 'hanging judge' George Jeffreys. However, this is not a cut-and-dried murder case.

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: Mark Gatiss brings the Christmas ghost story tradition back to life with The Dead Room, the tale of a long-running radio horror series of the same name. Simon Callow (Victoria & Abdul, Shakespeare in Love, Four Weddings and a Funeral) plays Aubrey Judd, the veteran presenter of the series and national treasure, who finds that he must adapt to changing times and tastes. But whatever happened to the classic ghost stories? The good old days?

programme.title: Alaska: Earth's Frozen Kingdom
programme.desc: Three-part series that looks at a year in Alaska, revealing the stories of pioneering Alaskans, both animal and human, as they battle the elements and reap the benefits of nature's seasonal gold rush.

programme.title: The Story of Scottish Art
programme.desc: The 18th century heralded the greatest blossoming of Scottish artistry in its history. The most powerful and influential figures in Britain clamoured to have their portraits painted by Allan Ramsey and Henry Raeburn, and their houses designed by Robert Adam. They stood in awe at the epic Highland landscapes of Horatio McCulloch and wept at the sensitive genre paintings of David Wilkie. Scots artist Lachlan Goudie explores how the intellectual revolution of the Enlightenment and the classical influence of the continent gave these artists the confidence and the inspiration to forge a whole new artistic landscape. From dusty storerooms of Edinburgh to the dazzling antiquities of ancient Rome, this is a journey of startling contrasts - between the past and the future, between the forces of reason and romance, between Presbyterian restraint and unfettered emotion. Out of the ashes of the Reformation, a new culture identity was beginning to emerge, and it was built on art.

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the quiz programme from Surrey University. The specialist subjects are venomous reptiles, the history of the Liberal Party since 1877, France in the 17th century and Tolkien's fiction.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson hosts the popular panel game of word definitions and deceptions. Team captains Frank Muir and Arthur Marshall are joined by guests Jane Lapotaire, Dr Robert Burchfield, Ruth Madoc and Melvyn Bragg.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team journey to La Palma, where giant new telescopes and cutting-edge science are opening extraordinary new windows to the universe.

programme.title: Joan Sutherland
programme.desc: Soprano Joan Sutherland talks to Bernard Levin and sings scenes from some of her most celebrated roles. With the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, led by Erich Gruenberg and conducted by Richard Bonynge.

programme.title: Metalworks!
programme.desc: Art historian and curator Tobias Capwell celebrates the great age of armour. Referencing the unstoppable rise of the Royal Almain Armoury at Greenwich, he tells the forgotten story of how Henry VIII fused German high technology with Renaissance artistry in the pursuit of one aim - to become the very image of the perfect knight. Using the talents of foreign craftsmen and his court artist Hans Holbein, Henry transformed himself into a living metal sculpture. His daughter Elizabeth I further exploited that image, making her courtiers parade before her in the most innovative and richly decorated works ever commissioned in steel.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC.

programme.title: Talking Movies
programme.desc: Talking Movies looks at the films that made waves at the BFI London Film Festival and the New York Film Festival in October. Tom Brook explores the film Elsinore, which contains a magnetic performance from Andrew Scott portraying the actor Ian Charleson, and is already being tipped for Oscar glory. Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine also made a big impression and we talk to the director as well as the cast from the festival red carpet. Wedaeli Chibelushi offers her thoughts on the new African drama Congo Boy and Emma Jones looks at Spanish film La Bola Negra, which has been earning rave reviews and is being talked about as a serious contender for the Best Film category at Academy Awards in 2027. Plus, we head to the USA for a look at the New York Film Festival which opened with the crime drama Paper Tiger. Other standout films there included the documentary Once Upon A Time in Harlem and Mike Leigh's Tender Loving Care.

programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?

programme.desc: Nigeria is known as the ‘giant of Africa’, and Clive heads to one of the continent's largest cities, Lagos. programme.title: Africa: From Reparations to Action
programme.desc: African Heads of State have gathered at the annual Elevate Africa Presidential Roundtable in Accra, Ghana, to examine how the push for reparations for the transatlantic slave trade can move from recognition and resolutions to meaningful action. In a special Focus on Africa roundtable discussion hosted by Waihiga Mwaura, leaders explore the role of African governments, the African Union, Caribbean partners, and the wider international community in advancing reparative justice. The conversation also looks ahead, asking how Africa can engage its young people in shaping the reparations agenda, strengthen ties with the diaspora, encourage investment and return migration, and create opportunities that support the continent's future development. Bringing together questions of historical accountability and future prosperity, the discussion challenges leaders to move beyond declarations and chart a practical path towards reparative justice and sustainable development.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Protests across Europe led by youth movements have drawn attention to the role of social media in spreading information and misinformation. Largely led by gen-Z, these protests have included references to films like The Hunger Games and The Avengers, and featured people in costumes taking part in 'aura battles', while memes of the demonstrations are shared online. Researcher Dr Nayana Prakash considers how online platforms, viral videos and AI-generated content are now an inextricable part of protest movements. After Russian TV sent a camera crew to report on a Welsh independence march, BBC Monitoring's Russia specialist Francis Scarr examines how Russian state media is reporting on independence movements across the world, and what this coverage reveals about the Kremlin's portrayal of European instability and decline. Filmmakers Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes reflect on their documentary One in a Million, which follows a Syrian family over ten years as they rebuild their lives after fleeing Aleppo. Centred on Israa, first seen aged 11, the film traces her journey through adolescence, marriage and motherhood as she navigates life between two cultures.

programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: Food enthusiast and baker Briony May Williams travels the length of Italy to ask: are Italians too fussy about their food? The United Nations cultural body Unesco has recently given the country's entire cooking tradition special status - that's everything from pasta to pizza, mozzarella to tiramisu. But many Italians have strong opinions about how, when and what to eat, and some unwitting faux pas from visitors can send purists into a frenzy. Briony meets the innovators adding controversial ingredients to pizza and new flavours to ice cream, and the traditionalists who want to keep things exactly as they are.

programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Would you let AI walk around your home? We explore the growing race to put humanoid robots into our homes and workplaces. We examine Meta's reported robot project, the rise of Chinese robot manufacturers, the privacy risks of machines that can see, hear and map our lives and whether robots are becoming Big Tech's next multi-trillion-dollar bet. Meta has reportedly built a humanoid robot called Max and, if Mark Zuckerberg gets his way, this could be the next frontier for artificial intelligence. After years of AI living on our screens, Silicon Valley is now racing to give AI a body, one that can see, hear, move through the world and interact with people in real life. Could a humanoid robot really become as common as a smartphone? Would you trust one to help around the house, care for an elderly relative, or perform tasks at work? And as companies spend hundreds of billions of dollars on AI, are robots the breakthrough the industry has been waiting for, or another expensive gamble destined to disappoint?

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Can Africa hold on to more of the wealth its metals and minerals are creating? Amid the rise of electric cars, data centres and the ‘electrification of everything’, a growing number of countries across the continent are putting restrictions on their raw materials. The Democratic Republic of Congo, Ghana and Zimbabwe are amongst those want to keep more of the jobs and prosperity they bring at home, but what will it take to succeed? The CEO of the International Council on Mining and Metals, Rohitesh Dhawan, warns there could be a chilling effect on new investments if the rules keep changing. However the African Development Bank’s chief economist, Kevin Urama, says Africa needs the jobs for its young people and that could benefit the rest of the world too. Plus, Ben Thompson hears from the CEO of Hitachi Energy, Andreas Schierenbeck, about exactly where the demand for electricity is coming from.

programme.title: TechXplore
programme.desc: BBC Tech journalist Paul Carter travels to Japan to showcase some Japanese moonshot innovations and meet the people behind them. Travelling across regions east and west of Tokyo, he reveals how advanced technologies are tackling global challenges - and how these ideas are flowing around the world. Japan faces issues such as climate change, energy insecurity, natural disasters, and an ageing population in especially acute ways. Paul discovers that these pressures have made the country a proving ground for some bold, high-impact solutions. In Ibaraki, he visits the world's largest operational fusion facility, now serving as a testbed for Europe's next era of clean energy. In Chiba, he explores mental-health technologies designed to help people not only live longer, but happier lives. In Kyoto, Paul experiences disaster-response innovations designed to help protect communities from extreme weather. And in Tohoku, he meets a new generation of AI-powered robots designed to support life on Earth - and, ultimately, beyond.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Jonathan Head reports from Thailand, where recent flooding has highlighted the growing challenges facing Bangkok. As climate change brings rising seas and more extreme weather across South East Asia, we examine why the Thai capital is among the region's most vulnerable cities. Plus: BBC Eye investigates the shadow war being fought inside Russia, speaking to two Russian men who claim to have secretly worked for Ukraine's intelligence services. Through rare first-hand accounts, we explore a clandestine world of covert operations, sabotage and espionage targeting military personnel and infrastructure far from the battlefield.

In this episode: Jonathan Head reports from Thailand, where recent flooding has highlighted the growing challenges facing Bangkok. As climate change brings rising seas and more extreme weather across South East Asia, we examine why the Thai capital is among the region's most vulnerable cities. Plus: BBC Eye investigates the shadow war being fought inside Russia, speaking to two Russian men who claim to have secretly worked for Ukraine's intelligence services. Through rare first-hand accounts, we explore a clandestine world of covert operations, sabotage and espionage targeting military personnel and infrastructure far from the battlefield.

programme.title: Africa: From Reparations to Action
programme.desc: African Heads of State have gathered at the annual Elevate Africa Presidential Roundtable in Accra, Ghana, to examine how the push for reparations for the transatlantic slave trade can move from recognition and resolutions to meaningful action. In a special Focus on Africa roundtable discussion hosted by Waihiga Mwaura, leaders explore the role of African governments, the African Union, Caribbean partners, and the wider international community in advancing reparative justice. The conversation also looks ahead, asking how Africa can engage its young people in shaping the reparations agenda, strengthen ties with the diaspora, encourage investment and return migration, and create opportunities that support the continent's future development. Bringing together questions of historical accountability and future prosperity, the discussion challenges leaders to move beyond declarations and chart a practical path towards reparative justice and sustainable development.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Protests across Europe led by youth movements have drawn attention to the role of social media in spreading information and misinformation. Largely led by gen-Z, these protests have included references to films like The Hunger Games and The Avengers, and featured people in costumes taking part in 'aura battles', while memes of the demonstrations are shared online. Researcher Dr Nayana Prakash considers how online platforms, viral videos and AI-generated content are now an inextricable part of protest movements. After Russian TV sent a camera crew to report on a Welsh independence march, BBC Monitoring's Russia specialist Francis Scarr examines how Russian state media is reporting on independence movements across the world, and what this coverage reveals about the Kremlin's portrayal of European instability and decline. Filmmakers Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes reflect on their documentary One in a Million, which follows a Syrian family over ten years as they rebuild their lives after fleeing Aleppo. Centred on Israa, first seen aged 11, the film traces her journey through adolescence, marriage and motherhood as she navigates life between two cultures.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina is rudely awakened to present this episode from Taunton in Somerset, where a huge antiques centre beckons for two teams of shoppers. In red are friends Aimi and Neil, and in blue are siblings Joe and Bella. With expert Ben Cooper by their side, the reds wonder whether they can cut a deal with an old knife box, while the blues and Danny Sebastian ponder over a wooden propeller – but aerospace engineer Joe doesn’t think it’ll fly at auction. In neighbouring Wiltshire, Christina visits the historic town of Malmesbury to learn about its ancient royal connections. In the abbey, she sees the tomb of the first king of England, Æthelstan, and pops next door to the Old Bell Hotel, which has been welcoming guests since 1220, including King Henry III in 1265. The hotel is now owned by a Texan businessman who has a surprising family connection to the guesthouse. At auction in nearby Chippenham, can auctioneer Tim Weeks make some right royal profits for the reds and blues?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Carl from Hull is our first visitor to Edinburgh’s historic Leith Theatre, selling some antique handcuffs from his personal collection. Who says crime doesn’t pay? Back to try her luck in front of the dealers once again is young Charlotte from Cambridge. She may have found her designer Paul Secon lampshade in a charity shop, but that doesn’t mean she’ll be giving it away... Shop display items are usually in demand, and it looks like Tracey has doubled her chances of a profit by bringing in two mannequin heads. Simon Bower and Nigel Havers are charmed, but how will Tracey get on when she faces the dealers? Joining us next from the west coast of Scotland is Robert, with an impressive concrete bust. It’s an imposing decorative piece, but questions over its antique appeal might mean bids are hard to come by. It may be more of a collectable curio than a working model these days, but if Brian focuses on the right buyer, his vintage camera is sure to be a moneymaker.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Paula, Ranie, Aaron and Pam – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: Sophie Raworth and Petroc Trelawny present live coverage from London as HM the King leads the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph. His Majesty will be joined on Whitehall by senior members of the royal family and leading UK politicians, alongside representatives of the armed forces, the Commonwealth and faith communities for the two-minute silence at 11 o’clock and the National Service of Remembrance. Survival depends entirely on the experience of their mother and how well they learn the skills she teaches them. With the help of bear expert Dr Lynn Rogers, Julia Bradbury explores the woods, learning about the lives of the black bears and the particular trials facing these three vulnerable little cubs. Sam, Sophie and Sybil must follow their mother's lead closely if they are going to survive in this tough and unforgiving wilderness, and make it through this critical month.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A pedestrian hurls himself at a car, then blames the driver. But the dashcam reveals a murkier story. In Widnes, horse rider Jayne Scotson films a frighteningly close pass, while in Liverpool, a van mounts the pavement to dodge a bin lorry, and could take out innocent bystanders. Police and fraud investigators reveal how footage recorded by ordinary people helps them uncover the truth and pursue justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion time travels back to the 70s in Nottinghamshire, and it all feels very familiar. Martin is loving his surroundings in Bath, and Jacqui sees beyond the work that needs to be done in Norfolk to appreciate the potential.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is patrolling the forecourt of Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester, hoping to find three items that are packed with potential and give them the chance to shine once more. She finds a pair of folding chairs, an old washstand and a collection of glass bottles. Upholsterer Simion Hawtin-Smith and upcycler Sarah Parmenter set to work helping Jacqui transform her finds, but will all three projects produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Having spent many happy family holidays in Cornwall, a couple from Hertfordshire now want to make England’s most south-westerly county their permanent home, and Steve Brown is just the man to help them realise their dream. The trio also meet a local ceramicist and take part in a pottery throwdown.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Martin, Robyn, Paul and Wayne – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

Tony is on a high after his team’s huge win over their big rivals last weekend and he’s proposing that their terrace anthem is the greatest of all time. The spicy pies are back and so are the spicy opinions as Hot Take returns for its second appearance of the season. Can the panellists take the heat or will their opinions be too hot to handle? programme.title: Scotland’s Sacred Islands with Ben Fogle
programme.desc: Ben Fogle explores the ancient sea roads of the Inner Hebrides, with their evocative connections to 6th-century Christian missionaries. On Tiree, Ben explores 1,300-year-old temple ruins. Although remoteness and Viking raids have obscured its history, an undeniable air of spirituality remains. Ben visits crofter Rhoda Meek, who balances farming life with a day job in IT. Julie Clarke left her life in Glasgow to escape a difficult upbringing and moved to the Isle of Coll, transitioning to a woman in the process. The island and its people gave her confidence and support. A highlight of Ben’s journey is a visit to Iona, the island after which he named his daughter. Ben ends his pilgrimage staying overnight in a shepherd's hut.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police uncover a huge cannabis haul in Inverness, search for a missing man in Glencoe, and face a siege after checking on a man believed to be in need of help.

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: On the Isle of Skye, fairy tales are more than just stories. From magical pools promising eternal youth, to ancient bridges said to connect our world with the supernatural, the island’s fairy folklore draws thousands of curious visitors every year. But is it all a clever tourist trap, or does something deeper lie behind the legends? In this enchanting adventure, sceptic Zara joins folklore enthusiast Evelyn to investigate the mysteries of Skye’s fairy tradition. At the heart of their journey is Dunvegan Castle’s legendary Fairy Flag, an ancient relic said to have been gifted by a fairy and to hold the power to protect the MacLeod clan in battle. As they uncover dramatic tales of clan warfare, explore Gaelic songs and hear extraordinary stories passed down through generations, Evelyn and Zara discover a tradition woven into the island’s history, identity and culture. Could there be more to the fairies of Skye than meets the eye? And will the promise of eternal youth finally tempt Zara to believe in a little magic?

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: Was Mary Queen of Scots responsible for her husband’s murder, or was she the victim of a ruthless plot to destroy her? Evelyn and Zara embark on a royal murder mystery to uncover the truth behind one of Scotland’s most infamous queens. From the shocking death of Lord Darnley to the mysterious Casket Letters, they follow a trail of scandal, suspicion and political intrigue, meeting historians who reveal the secrets behind the story. With affairs, betrayal and power-hungry nobles at every turn, the evidence raises serious questions about who really wanted Darnley dead. Was Mary a murderer, or was she framed by those determined to control her? As her story unfolds, a woman’s fight for power becomes a battle for her reputation, and the legacy she left behind.

programme.title: Disclosure
programme.desc: A single mum from Scotland's east coast embarks on a whirlwind romance with a Ghanaian preacher. They quickly marry, and she takes his side as the first lady of his church. But lives are torn apart when tragedy strikes. Reporter Myles Bonnar meets friends and family to try to find out what happened to Charmain.

programme.title: Disclosure
programme.desc: Reporter Myles Bonnar travels to Ghana to look into Charmain's death. There, he interrogates the police investigation that was carried out at the time, and meets those who were at the scene, as he searches for the truth about what happened in room 112.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die. As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated. Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death. Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales. Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height.

programme.desc: Kate Robbins presents this month’s Lifeline appeal on behalf of PMRGCAuk, a charity providing support, information and advocacy for people affected by polymyalgia rheumatica and giant cell arteritis.
