programme.desc: Game show in which 30 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher explores the food market in Hay-on-Wye, getting tips on growing food and finding out the secret to making fudge. Chef Julie Lin discovers bargains in world food stores and supermarket aisles, and food journalist Leyla Kazim lifts the lid on smoothies. Ryan Hand finds out how to get wood-fired pizza perfection in an oven.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Scottish railway journey reaches Aberdeen, from which he heads to the wild and beautiful Forvie National Nature Reserve and Scotland's most easterly town, Peterhead.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: A dolphin is about to be born in the treacherous waters of Shark Bay in Western Australia. Puck, the wise mother, must use all her skills to keep her newborn safe from the sharks that sweep into the bay every year. With the help of her close-knit family of females, she must teach the vulnerable baby dolphin the secrets of survival. From whistling to her unborn calf to the first few hours of baby Samu's life and the struggles her eldest son faces leaving home, this film provides a rare insight into the lives of bottlenose dolphins.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team return to Edinburgh in search of Scottish treasure. Amongst the items uncovered are an early Mickey Mouse mascot and a rare deco figurine.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Blackburn Cathedral in the heart of the town centre. The experts on duty today are Anita Manning and Philip Serrell. Anita values a gold charm bracelet, and Philip takes a shine to an unusual globe. Paul Martin learns about the remarkable life and work of classical singer Kathleen Ferrier.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Maisie Adam, Ade Edmondson, Rickie Haywood-Williams and Sammi Kinghorn take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is here with more Strictly exclusives and behind-the-scenes gossip ahead of the weekend. A fresh all-star panel is on hand to discuss the couples' next dances.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: President Trump says the 'Dumocrats' only have themselves to blame after a stock market panic over AI. Newsnight interviews a leading Democrat. And, a wave of hoax bomb threats has disrupted multiple European flights and forced the evacuation of newsrooms in Ireland, with authorities warning it is likely a 'coordinated campaign of disruption'. How serious is the threat? With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: The team investigates some of nature’s biggest mysteries: where have all the acorns gone? Just how small is Britain’s smallest bird? And do conkers really keep spiders away?

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the end of an era on Gardeners' World as Monty approaches his final programme from Longmeadow, the garden he has shared with the nation for the last 16 years. With Ned by his side, he celebrates the enduring pleasures of gardening and serves up one last bulb lasagne. Autumn is a busy time with vegetables to sow, perennials to plant and windfall apples to collect. Carol Klein takes a deep dive into the scientific world of plants. This time, it’s all about the magical properties of their shoots. Joe Swift visits close friend and garden designer Ann-Marie Powell to explore her own garden, a place that has become her solace since the death of her husband last year. In North Yorkshire, there’s a remarkable, pioneering woman on a quest to grow thousands of trees from seed. And a couple in East Grinstead share their combined love for the garden they have created together.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Gardener Monty Don traces his family tree. His efforts lead him to a port near Anglesey, where he learns of a national disaster that ended in a family tragedy.

programme.title: Planes, Trains and Automobiles
programme.desc: When bad weather grounds all planes, an uptight advertising man and a laid-back shower curtain ring salesman are thrown together by circumstance to travel against the clock and against the odds to get home to Chicago before Thanksgiving.

programme.title: Their Finest
programme.desc: 1940, London, the Blitz. With the country's morale at stake, Catrin, an untried screenwriter from Ebbw Vale, and a makeshift cast and crew work under fire to make a film to lift the nation's spirits - and inspire America to join the war. Leading the cast is the self-absorbed actor Ambrose Hilliard, who is persuaded to coach the handsome young American hero who has been 'parachuted' into the acting profession - but that will only be when the script is produced. Acclaimed period drama from BBC Films.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel. The film follows one mother who begins the year planning a future with her daughter, only to see it end with a promise to avenge her daughter’s death. After she publicly blamed the Iranian authorities, she was forced to flee the country and live in exile. A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death. Filmed both inside and outside the country, this is the raw and uncompromising story of a year in Iran, told by some of the people who were there.

programme.title: Sisters in Country: Dolly, Linda and Emmylou
programme.desc: How Dolly Parton, Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris's careers took off in the 1970s with distinct takes on country, and how they ended up uniting as close harmony singers on Trio.

programme.title: Aberfan: The Village That Fought Back
programme.desc: The collapse of a coal waste tip above the Welsh village of Aberfan in 1966 is one of the most devastating disasters in modern British history, killing 144 people. In the aftermath, a grieving community takes on the government, demanding justice and the removal of the huge tips still threatening the village. Their campaign confronts those in power and fights to prevent another disaster.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: When a jukebox washes up, its catchy song proves a hit among the Piripenguins, driving Pancake up the wall. A solution is needed, but how can he stop a seemingly unstoppable trend?

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: During a hoverboard race, Dad's new super-powered hoverboard malfunctions, so Cosima and Big Lizard throw the race to rescue him!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: It's mini mayhem when the ducklings find a device that can shrink things.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Blossom is terrible at keeping secrets, and Trevor can’t help but point that out. To prove him wrong, Blossom refuses to reveal the secret hiding place for her piece of the Amulet of Protection, even though the heroes need it to stop Balthazar casting a weather spell on the forest. With a rain of crabs heading their way, the heroes must quickly persuade Blossom to reveal her secret.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings catch a grasshopper that can give you whatever your heart desires.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck and Frog are DJs at a wedding, and Frog decides to liven things up with some banging tunes - much to the horror of Duck, the wedding planner and an angry father of the bride!

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Lacey challenges Ult with a special kind of training in the Terarium.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: While in Alfea, fairies and witches prepare for the self-defence test in the simulation chamber, and Bloom is paired with her rival Jasper. Tensions rise when Jasper makes a pact with the Trix.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: The Ultimate Bhangra dance team join Blue Peter, Shini and Hacker show viewers how to make decorations for Diwali, and Abby is off to France for a road trip adventure.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall heads to the cities of Chile in search of the wildlife surviving alongside people. From feisty sea lions to a giant bullfrog that needs protecting for its survival.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the end of an era on Gardeners' World as Monty approaches his final programme from Longmeadow, the garden he has shared with the nation for the last 16 years. With Ned by his side, he celebrates the enduring pleasures of gardening and serves up one last bulb lasagne. Autumn is a busy time with vegetables to sow, perennials to plant and windfall apples to collect. Carol Klein takes a deep dive into the scientific world of plants. This time, it’s all about the magical properties of their shoots. Joe Swift visits close friend and garden designer Ann-Marie Powell to explore her own garden, a place that has become her solace since the death of her husband last year. In North Yorkshire, there’s a remarkable, pioneering woman on a quest to grow thousands of trees from seed. And a couple in East Grinstead share their combined love for the garden they have created together.

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: The team investigates some of nature’s biggest mysteries: where have all the acorns gone? Just how small is Britain’s smallest bird? And do conkers really keep spiders away?

programme.title: Grand Hotel
programme.desc: During an eventful few days, the luxurious Grand Hotel in Berlin hosts the intersecting lives of a diverse group of guests, including a Russian ballerina fearful that her career is waning, a penniless baron, a terminally ill accountant and a powerful Prussian businessman desperate to make a deal. Classic star-studded drama from MGM studios.

programme.title: Ice Station Zebra
programme.desc: When a secret film capsule from a Russian spacecraft lands near Station Zebra, the tiny weather base is plunged into the Cold War and a confrontation between two super powers.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today, Flog It! comes from the Blickling Estate in north Norfolk. Five antiques experts are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. David Harper is excited by an early device for watching films, whilst David Fletcher and James Lewis reminisce about Rupert the Bear books and Dinky toys. Paul Martin enjoys a ride in a tank on a historic former military camp.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The second leg of the race takes the teams across the heart of Borneo to a modern metropolis on its eastern coast and their second checkpoint.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Live coverage of the FA Cup First Round tie between Altrincham of the National League and League One Notts County. One of the country’s most historic non-league clubs, Altrincham have a proud record of FA Cup giant-killing, having claimed 17 wins against league opposition, more than any other club that has never been part of the top four divisions. Now in the third tier, visitors Notts County are the world’s oldest professional league team, winning this illustrious trophy in 1894. They exited the competition to non-league opposition at this stage last season losing on penalties to Brackley Town. Jason Mohammad presents from Moss Lane.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: Of the calls the RNLI respond to every year, some are a race against the tide while others are against the weather. But all of them are a race against time. The crew at Tower, on the River Thames in London, are the busiest of all the lifeboat stations, averaging over 500 shouts a year and aiming to launch to any emergency in under 90 seconds. When a call comes in about a man in the water near the Thames Barrier, they reach him with just moments to spare. In Fleetwood, on the Lancashire coast, a desperate 999 call alerts the crew to a bait digger - out looking for worms on the sand flats - who has been caught out by the incoming spring tide and is in danger of being submerged and swept out to sea. And on the most southerly point of the Sussex coast, in Selsey, the crew race to the rescue of a local diver with a suspected case of ‘the bends’.

programme.title: 40 TV Theme Tunes at the BBC
programme.desc: A selection of 40 top title tracks which made such an impression on viewers that they made that difficult leap from TV schedules to the pop charts. Sometimes performed by members of the cast, sometimes featuring recognisable tracks from the big names of the day, these are the songs that have became essential tracks on the soundtrack to people's lives. Covering six decades and every genre of television, including comedies like Friends, The Office, Derry Girls and Absolutely Fabulous; dramas like Twin Peaks, Peaky Blinders, The Sopranos and Happy Valley; and much-loved classics, including the themes to M*A*S*H, Hill Street Blues, Doctor Who, and even Top of the Pops itself.

programme.title: Greatest BBC Music Moments
programme.desc: To celebrate 90 years of BBC Television, this is a deep dive into the vaults to find the unforgettable headliners, the raw talent, the historic nights and the songs that defined generations. From Pulp at the BBC Radio Theatre to Stormzy at Glastonbury’s Pyramid stage, join Dermot O’Leary, Jo Whiley and more of BBC’s musical curators as they bring you their Greatest BBC Music Moments.

programme.title: The Taste of Things
programme.desc: French romance set in 1889, focusing on the enduring bond between gourmet chef Dodin and his cook of 20 years, Eugénie. Having shared a passion for food and a deep mutual respect, the two have been lovers as well as gastronomers for a long time, but Eugénie has refused to marry Dodin, who resolves to cook for her in order to woo her.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: Cheryl returns to Liverpool with devastating news for Michael. With no way out, he is forced to make an impossible decision to protect the one he loves. Meanwhile, tensions rise among the Phelans as they hunt Banksey, unaware a new enemy is moving in the shadows.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: Four famous faces paired with a friend or a loved one must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo to the southern tip of Australia.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Mid Wales is today's destination on Christine Walkden's balloon tour of some of Britain's finest gardens. At Powis Castle Garden, she learns how to brace an ancient yew and meets David, whose family had worked there for generations. At the Dingle Garden, she helps to restore an obscured view. We also hear the story of Mona Holloway, a wartime land girl who found love on a neighbouring farm.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: At Forest Green Rovers, known as the ‘little club on the hill’, Vick Hope discovers how a team from a small Gloucestershire hamlet made it into the professional leagues, before trying her hand at mowing the pitch with the club’s groundsman. Matt Baker follows the journey of a locally brewed organic beer from barley field to pint glass and meets the greengrocer supplying fresh produce to the world’s first fully vegan football club. He then heads into the kitchen to see how that seasonal veg ends up on the players’ plates. Meanwhile, Adam Henson is on the lookout for two new signings of his own as he heads to Yorkshire to find some fresh recruits for his white park herd back in Gloucestershire.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads to the annual autumn calf sale in the historic Newton Stewart mart and finds out how this special building is still going strong over a century after it was built. Cammy is in Dumfries and Galloway, where he examines what the arrival of the bluetongue virus means for Scottish farmers and hears from the chief vet. Shahbaz is on the Morvern Peninsula, where she heads underground to explore Europe’s only silica sand mine. Ahead of Children in Need, Arlene is in the Borders, where she visits a charity near Selkirk that uses the healing power of horses. And Leanna is in North Sutherland finding out about community efforts to save the endangered great yellow bumblebee.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek is hunting down his most terrific treks from the south. His first quest is an adventure between two captivating castles - Caerphilly and Castell Coch, where he gets the chance to don a full suit of armour. Next, Derek is in Gower walking from Fall Bay to Oxwich, where he discovers a mysterious clifftop hideaway and learns how this area used to be a haven for smugglers. On the way, he tries abseiling, cold-water swimming and foraging for seaweed. The last walk Derek remembers is in the wonderful Wye valley, where he marvels at one of the UK’s first tourist walks, takes to the water in a canoe and visits the awe-inspiring Tintern Abbey, where he witnesses the relics of a remarkable archaeological excavation.

programme.title: Swallows and Amazons (2016)
programme.desc: Four children dream of escaping the tedium of a summer holiday with their mother. When finally given permission to camp on their own on an island in the middle of a vast lake in the Lake District, they are overjoyed. But when they get there, they discover they may not be alone. The battle for ownership of a lonely island teaches them the skills of survival, the value of friendship and the importance of holding your nerve. Based on the novel by Arthur Ransome.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: For a live demonstration of terroir, Eva heads to Domaine Dujac, home of the current most-wanted Burgundy wine. Standing on one side of a road, owner Jeremy Seysses points to a parcel of grand cru (the very best) of Clos de la Roche. On the other side is a premier cru (the next best) - a Gevrey-Chambertin Combottes. Back at the winery, Eva tucks into beef cheeks bathed in Domaine Dujac for a classic boeuf bourguignon lunch. Despite the grapes being grown just a few metres away, these reds are a class apart.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles presents from Kingston in Surrey, with the reds and the blues led by experts Thomas Forrester and Gary Pe. Both teams are eager to make a profit at the auction, but who will win? While the competition hots up, Eric gets on his bike at the Herne Hill Velodrome.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Tommy is by the seaside in the Norfolk village of Eccles-on-Sea to see a very unusual wooden property that he fears may be beyond salvation. He’s also in Islington, north London, living the high life at a two-bed flat situated on one of the upper floors of a high-rise building. Dion is in Sheffield to view an intriguing auction lot comprising three terraced houses.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Live coverage of the FA Cup First Round tie between Cray Wanderers of the Isthmian League and League One Stockport County. Recognised as London’s oldest football club - pre-dating the FA Cup itself - seventh-tier Cray are making their maiden appearance in the 1st Round. Alex Scott presents from Flamingo Park in Chislehurst.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Paris is home to more award-winning pastry chefs than anywhere else in the world. Here, the day revolves around patisserie. Morning begins with the buttery flakes of a croissant. At midday, a baguette tucked under the arm signals lunch. And by the afternoon, mouthwatering sweet treats are savoured like miniature works of art. Resistance is futile, and Eva is seduced by the Paris-Brest, a rum baba, the macaron, a mango cake and dahlia, to name just a few.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Jason Mohammad presents highlights from the first round of the FA Cup. London’s oldest club Cray Wanderers host Stockport County, who are flying high in League One, and non-league Stafford Rangers play Grimsby Town. 2021 FA Cup winners Leicester City travel to 6th tier Oxford City. Plus a full round-up of the weekend’s cup action.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Crystal Palace Park in south east London, where highlights include a diamond ring found wrapped up in a sock, a Louis Vuitton trunk and a surprise visit from a living artist. Will Farmer is delighted to see a pair of majolica whippets, while Jon Baddeley is stunned to discover a rare sundial by Thomas Tuttell that dates back to the end of the 17th century. Lee Young is intrigued by a trio of bronze Chinese censers bought from a flea market, while Ronnie Archer Morgan discovers clothing and correspondence with a direct link to Ethiopian ruler Haile Selassie. Fiona Bruce meets cartoonist Ralph Steadman, best known for his work with maverick American journalist Dr Hunter S Thompson, while Mark Smith challenges Fiona to identify secret Second World War spy gadgets concealed in everyday items. Clare Tole-Moir is thrilled to see a rare DIY kit dress by fashion designer Paco Rabanne, while John Foster admires a jointed wooden artist’s model with a surprising value.

programme.title: Remembrance Sunday: The Cenotaph
programme.desc: Highlights from the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson visits a small village in Northumberland to find out how the family and village who both share the name Craster have had their lives and fortunes intertwined for over 800 years. The village sits on a unique seam of rock called the Whin Sill and next to the North Sea. Ben learns how, through the generations, the Crasters have used local resources to make their fortunes and in turn have changed the face and the fortunes of the village and the villagers. Ben meets Michael Craster, who still lives in the family’s 850-year-old tower and is an expert on his ancestors. Ben follows the family tree and hears of various heads of the family, such as the Georgian period’s Daniel Craster who developed quarrying in the village.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture to the northernmost reaches of the UK – Shetland – to fish the lochs and the seas of this remote and beautiful place for trout and pollock. Shetland is an archipelago of about 100 islands off the north east coast of Scotland, only around 15 of which are inhabited. It feels like they have entered a very different world - and it's full of surprises for both of them.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: After a hair-raising drive across the Conor Pass and a spot of seaside silliness hitting golf balls into the ocean, Bill bids farewell to Chris O'Dowd. In County Clare, Bill and Tom's attempt to sneak unnoticed into a hurling match goes awry, before an emotional reunion recalls an unforgettable act of kindness. Then, a chance invitation in Ballybunion leads to a freezing Atlantic challenge.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools welcomes Jamie T, Antony Szmierek, Violet Grohl, Emily Bear, Tia Gordon and Leo Sayer to the show.

programme.title: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy
programme.desc: Film adaptation of John Le Carre's Cold War novel about a retired MI6 agent who must track down a Soviet mole within the British intelligence service's ranks.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Is the ‘politics of nastiness’ over following the Democrats sweeping the House and Senate in the US midterms, and what does it mean for the tone of politics in the UK and Europe? Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Liverpool, discussing immigration, the US midterms, the costs on small businesses and slavery reparations. On the panel: deputy leader of the Labour party Lucy Powell, Conservative Luke Evans, general secretary of the Trades Union Congress Paul Nowak, columnist and commentator at the Telegraph Tim Stanley and psychologist and ex-NBA star John Amaechi/

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: As Michael struggles to maintain control, Ozzie manipulates Freddie down a dark path.

programme.title: Ellie & Natasia
programme.desc: Two pregnant mums offer their unfiltered takes on the world of high fashion; eccentric characters take a walk down a very different kind of red carpet; Only Fools and Horses gets an all-female reimagining; a formidable lady claims to have made almost everything that's for sale in the world; a couple's attempt to spice things up in the bedroom goes horribly off the rails; and a serious break-up conversation is interrupted by an agonisingly delayed sneeze. Featuring a guest appearance by Kiell Smith-Bynoe.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The A to Z of TV Gardening
programme.desc: Carol Kirkwood takes an alphabetical journey through the world of gardening, getting inspiration and advice from some of the BBC's most popular garden presenters and programmes. In this episode, Carol explores subjects that all begin with the letter A, including apples, asparagus and alliums.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: Beyond the horizon lies the vast open ocean, a world teeming with extraordinary life where giant blue whales, tiny drifting crabs and tenacious turtles thrive against all odds.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights from five Premier League games, including Manchester United against Aston Villa and Liverpool’s trip to Crystal Palace. Sunderland take on Chelsea, Bournemouth travel to Ipswich and Brighton face Brentford. Presented by Kelly Cates.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Scotland’s gardeners have to work with a huge variety of challenging conditions. In this programme, we take a look at gardens and gardeners in the far corners of Scotland. From battling with the elements on the tip of Sutherland to a subtropical garden paradise in the Borders and growing with no soil, across the bridge over the Atlantic on the Island of Seil - these gardeners are all working on the very edges of Scotland.

programme.title: The Wooden Horse
programme.desc: Dramatisation of one of the most ingenious escape bids of World War II. In camp Stalag Luft III, the Nazis have built the prisoners' huts so far from the fence that underground escape is virtually impossible. One British officer, inspired by the tale of the Trojan Horse, proposes a daring plan to start a tunnel close to the boundary using a wooden vaulting horse as cover.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Normanby Hall, where finds include a marble bust gifted by a generous neighbour, valued at £15,000, and a pair of rare candlesticks won in a newspaper competition.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today, Flog It! comes from Dover Castle in Kent. Antique experts Catherine Southon and Jonathan Pratt search for items to take off to auction. Catherine falls for a colourful brooch and Jonathan unearths a horn beaker used by Winston Churchill. Paul Martin uncovers the story of Dover Castle’s secret tunnels.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor kicks off a new week by chatting exclusively to the latest couple to be eliminated from the competition. Also, Friday’s all-star Panel return for a deep dive into the weekend’s action.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Akisa Wandera reports from Angola, where billions of dollars are being poured into a vast new trade corridor at the centre of a global race for critical minerals. We examine what's at stake for the people living on the frontline of this transformation. Plus: BBC Brasil travels to the city of Camaçari, where Chinese carmaker BYD has opened its biggest factory in Latin America. As Chinese investment reshapes jobs, industry and daily life, we explore how one Brazilian city has become a test case for the growing rivalry between China and the United States.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy, the history of the English longbow, the television sitcom Brooklyn Nine-Nine and the record-breaking Paralympian Sir Lee Pearson.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Two teams return. It’s always nice to see them, but there’s no room for sentiment, because the winners progress to the next round while the losers exit the tournament. programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: It’s estimated that as many as 250 million sharks are taken from the world’s oceans every single year. Around 73 million of those are taken purely for their fins which are used in shark fin soup, with the rest of the body wasted. This fishing is causing the possibility of extinction for sharks - so, what can we do? First of all, learn about the fish you eat. Fish such as tuna and swordfish are caught with a very high bycatch of shark, which means sharks are caught accidentally when fishing for species. Look for sustainably caught fis, and if in doubt stay clear of it. Be aware of the things that are sold in your local fish and chip shop, as often things that are labelled as huss or rock salmon could actually be shark. And learn to love sharks! Having people understand that sharks are not the menacing, man-eating monsters they are made out to be is so important. Perhaps dream of diving with sharks yourself one day. With our help, sharks can survive into the future.

programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how allotments play an important role in the environment. They find out why they are great places to grow fruit and vegetables, explore a compost heap where worms and birds live and spot a water butt which recycles rainwater! On the way, they enjoy the peace and quiet of the allotment, before planting some potatoes!

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Today, Maddie is having a fun day out. She uses a special thermal camera at an ice rink to find out how runny water freezes to make solid ice we can skate on. Next, Maddie heads to a bouncy castle factory to see how a bouncy castle is made from lots of different coloured pieces of material sewn together. She then has a go at bouncing when the finished jungle-themed bouncy castle is inflated and brought to life.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that are all forms of transport! Grace drives a double decker bus, shows off an ice sled that is like a bus on ice, and then takes an electric Hackney carriage for a spin.

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: Solomon and his friends are practising letters with Miss Gerrard. Outside, the children are going to the climbing wall area, and Mrs Collins has a challenge for them. Later, Solomon and Lusungu get arty and make their very own tie-dye t-shirts to wear, with help from Mrs Farrell.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. A timid sperm whale must conquer his fears and dive deep down to help the Octonauts release Peso from a giant clam.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter accidentally sends a slumbering Mr Tolly floating off to Owl Island, he immediately launches a rescue with his friends.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The shadow of a monster causes panic among the Piris, apart from Nugget, who is keen to investigate a new mystery. She finally tracks down the creature, but is all exactly as it seems?

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: It’s the Tin Can Games, and Evil Pea wants to win the Tin Can trophy. She cheats in the final race by putting a magnet on Supertato’s back to stop him from going super fast.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The Ducklings are frustrated with Weasy - he always plays video games and leaves the attic in a mess! They notice that the farmer takes great care of his chickens and decide to live with him instead.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo needs to deliver a pizza to a very hard-to-reach island, but some stubborn seabirds have their eye on the pizza. Will Mojo have to go supersonic to get past them?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is excited to get her own room. But when bedtime comes, she misses her sister Bingo.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo are playing the quiet game so won't tell Dad which toy to buy for Muffin.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: The rock monster runs riot in the forest, scaring all the other creatures. The doctors must find out what’s causing him so much pain.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: PC Plum is determined to perform Great-Granny Plum’s song at the Balamory ceilidh all by himself, but he soon realises it isn’t easy being a one-man band.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi’s wish to have her toys tidy her bedroom turns into a search and rescue when one goes missing, and with Stuffy’s help she discovers tidying together works best.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran meet Isaiah and his daddies at the concert hall. They are there to hear a special concert – the orchestra are going to play Captain Chloe music and Isaiah’s daddy Joshua has a special clarinet solo. JoJo loves finding out about the orchestra and can’t wait to hear more of the Captain Chloe musical story. During the interval, they discover that Joshua is bit nervous about his solo. It's a good job that daddy Anton has baked good-luck biscuits for everyone to enjoy. The tannoy announces that the concert is about to begin again – the conductor is on stage, and the orchestra is ready to play. Soon it will be time for Joshua’s solo.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah and Duck are trying to exercise, but the neighbours need their help.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Major Clanger makes a new garden trolley for Mother, and when she accidentally wheels it over his foot, it turns out to be more useful than he could ever have imagined!

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa find a stripy sock and pretend it’s a caterpillar. On the Play Tree, they play with puppets and stage a show. When MeMo and BaBa are 'yummy-sized', the Yummies find another way to put on a show with the puppets. There is time for a final sleepy show on the Lullaby Lake before heading to Gramma Leeba and the Bay of Books.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Tombliboo Eee becomes separated from the other two Tombliboos, Unn and Ooo. They wander all over the garden looking for each other until Tombliboo Eee meets Upsy Daisy, who calls for the others with her megaphone.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Chris and Rosie Ramsey read the hilarious story of a cat in search of a place to sit.
